title: Normal ambient power-series rings and Cohen hypersurfaces
statement: Let $d\geq0$ be an integer. In either of the following cases form a commutative ring $S$. (i) Let $k$ be any field and put $S=k[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. (ii) Let $p$ be a prime and let $C$ be a Cohen ring with maximal ideal $pC$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Put $A=C[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ and $\mathfrak n=(p,X_1,\ldots,X_d)A$. Let $\Theta\in A$ have constant coefficient exactly $p$, and put $S=A/(\Theta)$. In case (ii), $\Theta\in\mathfrak n\setminus\mathfrak n^2$. In both cases $S$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] and a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], meaning a nonzero integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field. No perfectness hypothesis is imposed on $C/pC$. The case $d=0$ is included: $S=k$ in (i) and $S=C/pC$ in (ii).

In (ii) it gives that $A$ is regular local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=(p,X_1,\ldots,X_d)A$. The theorem allows every field and every Cohen ring, including imperfect residue fields and $d=0$.

proof.text: In (ii), apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-hypersurface-criterion] to the regular local ring $(A,\mathfrak n)$ and $f=\Theta$. Step 2 verifies both $f\in\mathfrak n$ and $f\notin\mathfrak n^2$. Therefore $S=A/(\Theta)$ is regular local. Together with step 1, this proves regular localness in both cases.

source.place: Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), regular local quotients by a member of a minimal parameter system

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak m$ be the maximal ideal of $S$, now regular local in either case. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], $S$ is a regular ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal], every prime localization is a normal domain, in particular $S_{\mathfrak m}$. The canonical map $S\to S_{\mathfrak m}$ is an isomorphism: every $s\notin\mathfrak m$ is a unit, and the inverse sends $a/s$ to $as^{-1}$; the defining equality of fractions makes this well defined and both composites are the identity. Consequently $S$ is a nonzero domain. This isomorphism also identifies the fraction fields: send $a/b$ to the quotient of the images of $a$ and $b$. A monic equation over $S$ maps to the same equation over $S_{\mathfrak m}$, so integral closedness there implies integral closedness in $S$. This proves exactly the normal-domain condition of [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].

proof.text: For $d=0$, [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] identifies the series ring with its coefficient ring. Thus (i) is $S=k$. In (ii) the sole coefficient of $\Theta$ is $p$, so $\Theta=p$ and $S=C/pC$. No step required any condition on Frobenius of $C/pC$, so no perfectness hypothesis is used.
